note: Suggestions only. Nothing on this list has been implemented. Choose a path (or reject) before any change is made. Each suggestion names the data it needs and how it can be verified.

suggestions.title: Add an official depth-chart table per team (starter, first backup, second backup)
suggestions.what: Build one row per team per position with the depth-chart order from the NFL.com team depth chart, plus the injury status of each listed player.
suggestions.why: Directly answers 'which backup replaces which starter' for offense and defense. Without this, unit exposure counts overstate or understate impact.
suggestions.data_needed: NFL.com team depth chart page (URL not yet confirmed - see Q6).
suggestions.risk: Depth chart format may change; needs per-page verification.
options: A: Build now for all 32 teams
B: Build for 4 teams first as a pilot
C: Skip for now; use counts only

suggestions.title: Separate 'Not injury related' absences from injury analysis
suggestions.what: Show the four non-injury absences (Bates, Davis, Al-Shaair, Garrett) in their own column, excluded from injury counts.
suggestions.why: Resting and personal-matter absences are not injury signals and would distort injury exposure.
options: A: Exclude from counts, show separately
B: Keep in counts with a marker

suggestions.title: Add a daily refresh with a last-verified date on every page
suggestions.what: Re-run the Week 10 data pull and rebuild the site on a fixed schedule; show the fetch date on every table.
suggestions.why: Injury statuses change before kickoff; a stale table can mislead decisions.
suggestions.data_needed: Scheduled job (GitHub Actions) and repo permission to run it.
suggestions.risk: Automated scraping of NFL.com must follow their terms; needs your approval.
options: A: Manual refresh each game day
B: Scheduled refresh (needs approval)

suggestions.title: Get a licensed odds archive before any line-making work
suggestions.what: Choose one odds source with historical closing lines and confirm its licence terms.
suggestions.why: Closing line value and ROI cannot be measured without real odds. No official NFL odds source exists.
suggestions.effort: Depends on vendor; may have cost.
options: A: Use nflverse schedule line fields (community source, check terms)
B: Licensed odds vendor
C: Defer odds work; do analysis of injuries and schedules first

suggestions.title: Start strategy research with spreads only
suggestions.what: Limit the first strategy round to point-spread bets; add totals, moneylines, props, and parlays later.
suggestions.why: Spreads need the fewest data types. Props and parlays add correlation and data problems that are hard to validate early.
suggestions.effort: Low for scope; High for validation.
suggestions.risk: Narrow scope may find fewer signals.
options: A: Spreads only first
B: Spreads + totals
C: All markets at once (not recommended)

suggestions.title: Adopt the validation gates before any strategy is ranked
suggestions.what: Use the gates listed on the Strategy page (provenance, out-of-sample, minimum sample, closing line value, correlation check, multiple-testing correction, season stability).
suggestions.why: Without gates, a leaderboard rewards luck. The gates are the mechanism to separate skill from variance.
suggestions.risk: Strict gates may produce no winners. That is a valid outcome.
options: A: Adopt all gates as written
B: Adopt, with your edits to thresholds

suggestions.title: Define the leaderboard reward before building it
suggestions.what: Decide whether rewards are site points, a published ranking, or nothing else.
suggestions.why: A money reward changes legal and responsible-gambling requirements.
suggestions.risk: Unclear reward definitions cause scope creep.
options: A: Points on the site only
B: Ranking with no reward
C: Money reward (requires legal review first)

suggestions.title: Add responsible-gambling guardrails if any wagering use is planned
suggestions.what: Set stake caps, loss limits, and a plain-language warning on any page that shows bets or strategies.
suggestions.why: Reduces harm if the analysis is used for real wagering.
suggestions.data_needed: Your bankroll and limits (Q10); official Mexican guidance (Q1).
suggestions.risk: None, if done before any strategy is shown.
options: A: Add guardrails now
B: Add only if wagering use is confirmed

suggestions.title: Use one source for each data type and record the source per row
suggestions.what: Keep NFL.com as the primary source; mark any community source (e.g., nflverse) as secondary on every row that uses it.
suggestions.why: Mixed sources without labels make verification hard.
options: A: Adopt (already applied to this site)
B: Change

suggestions.title: Add a weekly injury history table to test whether 'Questionable' predicts play
suggestions.what: Store each week's report and track how often Questionable and Doubtful players actually play.
suggestions.why: Turns injury designations into a measurable signal instead of an assumption.
suggestions.data_needed: Weekly NFL.com injury reports for past seasons (Q5).
suggestions.risk: Playing status needs a verified source for each game (box scores).
options: A: Collect from the 2026 season first
B: Collect multiple past seasons

suggestions.title: Consolidate the two dashboards into one site
suggestions.what: Two sessions published overlapping sites: the root 'Fourth & Signal' site (session 4a77261b) and the Week 10 data dashboard in docs/ (session d263eab0). Choose one structure, one navigation, and one source register.
suggestions.why: Duplicate pages (suggestions, strategies, flagged items) can disagree. A single owner for each page avoids conflicts between sessions.
suggestions.data_needed: Your choice of the primary site.
suggestions.risk: Moving pages changes URLs that may already be shared.
options: A: Keep both; cross-link (current state)
B: Make the root site primary and move docs/ pages into it
C: Make docs/ primary and retire the root pages
